goal: Make Debian 13 trixie the Linux GitHub Actions execution baseline.
description: Keep the blocking Linux repository gate executing inside a Debian 13 trixie container so the CI toolchain matches the documented development baseline. The hosted runner may only provide the container host.

acceptance_criteria.text: The blocking Linux repository gate runs its commands inside a debian:trixie container.
Docs state that the GitHub hosted runner is not the toolchain baseline and that Debian 13 trixie is the execution environment.

commit.message: Align CI with Debian trixie baseline

goal: Freeze the shared release platform key matrix.
description: Define the supported release platform keys for macOS arm64, Linux arm64, Linux x86_64, musl Linux x86_64, and Windows amd64 in release docs, doctor behavior, installer behavior, and managed styio release-target mapping.

acceptance_criteria.text: Release docs list darwin-aarch64, linux-aarch64, linux-musl-aarch64, linux-x86_64, linux-musl-x86_64, and windows-x86_64.
spio and styio release target namespaces are documented for Linux, macOS CLI, and Windows CLI artifacts.

commit.target: release docs and spio foundation plan

goal: Add GitHub-hosted Linux, macOS, and Windows CI lanes.
description: Split the repository CI surface into Linux, macOS, and Windows jobs. Linux remains the blocking Debian 13 gate, macOS runs native CMake build and tests, and Windows runs a non-blocking native adaptation smoke until the Windows port closes.

acceptance_criteria.text: local-ci-gate has a Linux Debian 13 job that runs the blocking repository gate.
local-ci-gate has a macos-latest job that configures, builds, and runs native tests with CMake.
local-ci-gate has a windows-latest job that attempts a native x64 CMake build and records Windows adaptation failures without blocking the Linux gate.

goal: Define the platform compatibility contract and evidence format.
description: Keep the three-platform final state, target matrix, CI lane policy, and real-machine evidence template in the spio foundation plan so all platform agents validate the same support contract.

acceptance_criteria.text: The spio foundation plan states that Linux, macOS, and Windows converge on one native implementation with OS-specific code only at runtime responsibility boundaries.
Evidence-Template.md records machine identity, build/test evidence, installer evidence, managed styio evidence, clean project workflow evidence, and failure notes.

goal: Make platform identity and executable naming a shared native boundary.
description: Replace ad hoc platform detection and executable path assumptions with one current native boundary that covers release platform keys, executable suffixes, managed styio paths, SPIO_HOME resolution, platform override tests, and doctor payloads for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

acceptance_criteria.text: Release platform detection has tests for darwin-aarch64, linux-aarch64, linux-musl-aarch64, linux-x86_64, linux-musl-x86_64, and windows-x86_64.
Managed styio and spio executable paths resolve to styio/spio on Unix and styio.exe/spio.exe on Windows without call-site string duplication.
spio doctor reports platform key, release target, executable path, SPIO_HOME, and release-root status consistently on all three OS families.

commit.target: src/SpioCore, src/SpioTool, src/SpioApp, and native tests

goal: Make native test declarations portable across all platform CI lanes.
description: Replace bash-only CTest declarations and POSIX-only test helpers with portable native or Python-backed checks while keeping the same CLI behavior assertions. Unix shell integration tests may remain Unix-only only when they validate the Unix installer contract.

acceptance_criteria.text: CTest can configure a Windows build with SPIO_BUILD_TESTS=ON without requiring bash for core CLI, manifest, resolver, doctor, toolchain, and workflow tests.
Unix installer shell tests remain scoped to Linux/macOS and have explicit CTest labels or conditions.
macOS and Linux native CTest runs still execute the existing behavior assertions after the portable test rewrite.

goal: Publish and verify the expanded three-platform artifact matrix.
description: Publish spio and managed styio artifacts for every announced platform key, verify SHA-256 sidecars, run spio doctor, and collect clean-machine workflow evidence before support is announced.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every announced platform key has spio and styio artifacts, channel pointers, SHA-256 sidecars, doctor evidence, and install smoke evidence.
Release docs mark only verified targets as supported and keep unverified targets out of public support claims.
Artifact layout uses tools/spio, tools/styio-linux, tools/styio-macos-cli, and tools/styio-windows-cli consistently.

commit.target: release docs, package roots, and evidence records

goal: Promote all platform CI lanes and support docs to the final compatibility policy.
description: After real-machine evidence and artifacts exist, make Linux, macOS, and Windows compatibility checks required where appropriate, remove the Windows non-blocking status, and align support claims, verification matrix, and post-push CI monitoring docs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Windows CI no longer uses continue-on-error after Windows native build, tests, installer, and workflow evidence are complete.
Post-commit CI docs and verification matrix name the Linux, macOS, and Windows checks that must be watched or required for platform support.
README and release checklist announce only platform keys with complete evidence records.
